title: Keyboard Manager: remaps with alt as the only modifier key have to be pressed twice before it work

status.label: Investigate Grab And Move modifier interference
status.detail: The author says disabling Grab And Move restores an Alt-only Keyboard Manager remap; related reports describe similar Alt/Win shortcut interference, including a 0.100.2 reproduction.

judgment.rationale: The report gives a concrete Alt+V-to-Ctrl+V remap and says the final key is inconsistently delivered while Grab And Move is enabled; disabling Grab And Move appears to restore normal behavior. Discussion adds a related Win+Space/Command Palette symptom and points to other Grab And Move hook reports. Issue #47585 has a reported reproduction on PowerToys 0.100.2. This supports a focused shared-input investigation, although this report's exact Grab And Move activation modifier and current-version behavior remain unconfirmed.
evidence: The report lists PowerToys 0.99.1 and says the behavior occurs with Grab And Move enabled; disabling it appears to fix the Alt-only remap.
The reported example is Alt+V to Ctrl+V, where the final key may need to be pressed twice or may fail.
A commenter says re-enabling Grab And Move does not reproduce the problem again until PowerToys restarts.
Another commenter reports a Win+Space Command Palette shortcut needing an extra key press when Grab And Move uses the Windows key.

Issue #47585 reports Win-key shortcut interference with Grab And Move and a reproduction on PowerToys 0.100.2; issue #47271 was closed by its reporter after identifying Grab And Move as the trigger, while #47337 describes a related Alt-first shortcut case.
judgment.recommended_action: Trace Grab And Move's modifier suppression/replay and hook ordering against Keyboard Manager and other global shortcuts, after confirming the exact activation modifier and current-version reproduction.

fix_assessment.rationale: The issue isolates Grab And Move as a condition, and related reports describe Alt/Win shortcut events losing their expected effect. The shared input-hook mechanism is plausible but has not been traced in code.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve unrelated Alt and Win shortcuts in Grab And Move
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Grab And Move may consume or replay Alt/Win key events while deciding whether a drag action is occurring, leaving Keyboard Manager or another global-shortcut consumer with an incomplete modifier/key sequence.
plan: Reproduce the Alt-only remap with Grab And Move enabled and record the selected activation modifier and relevant hook state.
Trace Grab And Move's handling of modifier and key-down/key-up events when no drag action is committed, including its interaction with Keyboard Manager's hook.

If unrelated shortcuts lose or receive reordered events, adjust the suppression/replay path so Grab And Move only intercepts the sequence it owns and other registered shortcut consumers receive a consistent event pair.
Add regression coverage for Alt+V to Ctrl+V with Grab And Move using Alt, and for a Win+Space global shortcut with Grab And Move using Win.
verification: The first Alt+V press produces exactly one Ctrl+V action with Grab And Move enabled.
Unrelated Alt- and Win-based shortcuts continue to work when Grab And Move does not activate a drag.
Grab And Move still starts and completes drag operations correctly, and toggling its activation modifier does not leave stale key state until restart.

confidence.rationale: The report identifies Grab And Move as a condition, and related open reports show similar Alt/Win shortcut interference. The exact event-loss mechanism and activation-modifier conditions have not been traced or confirmed on current stable.

issue_context.summary: An Alt-only Keyboard Manager remap may require a repeated key press when Grab And Move is enabled; disabling Grab And Move reportedly restores normal behavior.
known_information: The report lists PowerToys 0.99.1 from the Microsoft Store.
The example remap is Alt+V to Ctrl+V, with the final key sometimes needing to be pressed twice or failing.
The reporter says turning Grab And Move off seems to fix the behavior.
A commenter reports that re-enabling Grab And Move does not reproduce the issue again until PowerToys restarts.
A different commenter reports a Win+Space Command Palette shortcut needing an extra key press when Grab And Move uses the Windows key.
Related issues include #47585 (Win-key shortcut interference), #47271 (closed by its reporter after identifying Grab And Move), and #47337 (Alt-first shortcut behavior).
inferences: Grab And Move may be consuming, suppressing, or replaying a modifier/key event sequence needed by another shortcut handler.
The Alt-only remap and Win-key reports may share an input-hook state or event-ordering problem, but a common code path has not been verified.
issue_context.analysis: The report supports a focused investigation because disabling Grab And Move changes the outcome. Keep this issue distinct from the related reports until code tracing confirms a shared defect. Verify the exact Grab And Move activation key and current stable behavior before implementing a change.
initial_investigation: Read the current issue body and all five comments; verified there are no assignees.
Read the related current reports #47585, #47271, and #47337 to compare their Alt/Win shortcut symptoms and status.
Confirmed #47585 has a community-reported reproduction on PowerToys 0.100.2, while #47271 was closed by its reporter and #47337 remains a separate open Alt-first report.

information_gaps.information: Whether Alt-only remaps still fail on current stable and which activation modifier is selected in Grab And Move
information_gaps.why_needed: This confirms the report remains current and determines whether the suspected Alt or Win interception path should be investigated.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: On current stable, test Alt+V to Ctrl+V with Grab And Move enabled, report its selected activation modifier, and compare the result after disabling Grab And Move.

actions.label: Approve the Grab And Move input fix

comment.body: Thanks for identifying that disabling Grab And Move appears to restore the Alt+V-to-Ctrl+V remap. Could you confirm whether this still reproduces on current stable, and which activation modifier is selected in Grab And Move when it happens? That will distinguish the Alt-activation path from the related Win-key shortcut reports.
